9-23-19 I worked on unit 2 on compressor 2 circuit. Performed leak search on unit. Leak checked entire unit and found leak on distributor tube going into evap coil. Need to take a panel off to be able to get torch to location of leak. Will return to repair leak and recharge unit.    9-24-19. Returned to site and removed last bit of 410a that was in circuit 2 in unit. Removed all panels needed to access evap coil and get to leak. Cleaned paint off of piping and was able to braze pipe where leak was. Picked up nitrogen at supply house and pressure tested system. Pressures held over an hour and no leak found at joint. Removed nitrogen and evacuated circuit to 400 microns. Put all panels back on and then recharged system with 410a. Ran circuit all ok at this time.    9-24-19. While onsite at facility, customer asked for me to check alarm on last unit. Went to unit and found it in alarm with a current sensor board failure compressor A1. Checked board and found that board was not operating anymore and would need replacing. Informed customer that I would order a new board and correct issue on unit.    Arrived onsite and checked in with the customer. Went to rooftop of building and arrived at rooftop unit. Shutdown power to unit and performed LOTO to unit. Checked unit for power and then removed current sensing board that needed replacement. Replaced board with new board to complete replacement. Restored power back to unit after installing new board. Started up unit and began monitoring unit. Informed customer that job was completed and unit was fully operational.

Checked vacuum on B circuit, found at 565 microns. Turned off vacuum pump and performed a standing vacuum test. Held there for 45 minutes. Charged unit with 44 lbs of 410A, started B circuit. Checked pressure and temperatures and operation, operation of unit ok this time.

Circuit B out of gas (DOA). Found leak on distributor line. Patched with silfos and pressure tested for 24hrs. Swept with nitrogen and pulled vacuum, vacuum stalled at 2000 microns. Suspecting a pin hole. Changed dries as well. Suspect oil is saturated with water due to system being open. Oil requires replacing as well.    Resolution: Repair leak charge with refrigerant and change oil.
